clue.text: Quote this writer — rolling it will make you sick

indicators.note: rolling the phrase over turns it round so it is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it
the setter referring to themself

explanation.surface: A writer's quotation is so nauseating that turning it over in your mind turns your stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance taken to induce vomiting, so it is something that will make you sick.

clue.text: Travelling man — he had toothpaste forgetting all hotels will provide basics

indicators.note: travelling suggests letters on the move, rearranged into a new order
forgetting means these letters are left out of the pool before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
H is the radio-alphabet letter for hotel, and all of them means every H in the fodder, three in total

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman forgets toothpaste, but hotels will supply the essentials.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip every H from MAN HE HAD TOOTHPASTE (there are three) and rearrange the fifteen letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat and potatoes is an idiom for the fundamental, essential parts of something.

clue.text: Dish that is supporting good health for example

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so it is written second

parts.note: 'Good health!' is a toast raised with drinks
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A dish is said to support good health, as an example of healthy eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a toasted sandwich, a British snack dish.

clue.text: Lookout boasts note is in French

parts.note: to crow is to boast
N is an abbreviation for note
est is French for 'is'

explanation.surface: A lookout brags that a note is written in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow's nest is the lookout platform high on a ship's mast.

clue.text: Oddly Boeing suspect images released by police will generate profits

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd-numbered positions only

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word
E-FITs are computer-generated likenesses of suspects issued by British police

explanation.surface: A Boeing suspect's pictures, put out by police, will bring in money.
explanation.walkthrough: An E-FIT is the UK police's electronic facial composite, like a photofit.
explanation.definitionFit: Benefits as a noun are advantages or gains, which is what profits are.

clue.text: Critical report is, theoretically, what started it all

parts.note: a big moment is a critical one
a report is the sound of an explosion or gunshot

explanation.surface: A critic's report is held up, in theory, as the origin of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Bang is the scientific theory of how the universe began.

clue.text: Kitchen appliance brand delivered some cumin in jars

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word, the second word, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget maker sends out a spoonful of cumin in jars.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninja is a brand of blenders, air fryers and other kitchen gadgets.

clue.text: Officer seen intermittently when following street parties

indicators.note: coming after something means it is written after it
seen only at intervals means every other letter shows

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of the word
St is the abbreviation for street
as can mean 'when', as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A police officer is spotted now and then after street parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiestas are festivals or celebrations, particularly in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: This suggests it's safe at all times

definitions.meaning: surface reading: some sign or assurance of security
setter's reading: a phrase that looks like a numerical safe combination yet means round the clock, every hour of every day

explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads like the numbers of a safe's combination, while as a phrase it means continuously.
explanation.definitionFit: The numeric expression means all day every day, describing something available continuously without a break.

clue.text: Accompany Filipino getting a little nipple piercing

indicators.note: a piercing goes right through, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Tagalog is the main language of the Philippines

indicators.note: just a little of a word is its first letter

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Filipino person gets a small nipple piercing, with a friend along for support.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag along is a phrasal verb for going with someone, often uninvited.

clue.text: Another news report adds detailed advice taking just seconds as required

indicators.note: only the second letter of each word is taken

parts.words: Another news report adds detailed advice
parts.note: second letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: A further news bulletin adds detailed guidance, and in only seconds, as was necessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed and required are synonyms meaning necessary or called for.

clue.text: Fixed quickly

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a repair done in a hurry, but the two words are independent meanings of one adjective and adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means secure and immovable, as in holding fast, and also rapid or rapidly.

clue.text: Alice tattoos over old unwanted snakes — one points towards bottom?

indicators.note: snakes as a verb means winds about, signalling the letters are rearranged
unwanted means these letters are thrown out of the pool

parts.note: taken as written
O is the cricket abbreviation for over and a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Alice gets snake tattoos inked over old designs she no longer wants, one pointing down to her rear.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the two Os out of ALICE TATTOOS and rearrange the ten letters left. The definition plays on bottom: a stalactite hangs from a cave roof, its tip pointing to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalactite is an icicle-shaped mineral deposit hanging downward from a cave ceiling.

clue.text: Stick of dynamite originally hidden in a present

indicators.note: something hidden in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a, plus here meaning present, as in answering a register

indicators.note: originally points to how the word begins, its first letter

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A stick of dynamite is concealed inside a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to something, as glue does.

clue.text: Become less demanding of used piano

parts.note: used up and finished means gone
piano is the musical direction for playing softly

explanation.surface: Someone eases off their demands on a second-hand piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To go soft is an idiom for becoming lenient or easing standards.

clue.text: Dregs of society of no significance according to Spooner: twerp!

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don famed for swapping the opening sounds of words, signals that the first sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: scum means the lowest, most worthless people
null means having no value or effect

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the lowest of society as worthless and calls them an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of SCUM and NULL: the N sound goes to the front of the first, the SK sound to the second, giving NUMB and SKULL as heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbskull is a stupid person, much as a twerp is a silly, contemptible one.

clue.text: Laptop loses power for minute — one might need drive to work?

definitions.text: one might need drive to work?

indicators.note: losing one thing in exchange for another means one letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a laptop is a portable computer
P is the physics symbol for power; it comes out
M is the abbreviation for minute; it goes in its place

explanation.surface: A laptop runs out of power for a minute, and needs its drive to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'drive' to be a computer's disk drive; it is a car journey to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A commuter travels regularly to and from work, often driving there.

clue.text: Maybe pawn silver here with no limits for organiser

parts.note: a pawn is an example of a man, a chess piece
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: no limits means the first and last letters are taken off

parts.note: the inner letters of here are taken

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker's shop is suggested as the place to hock silver.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess any piece, pawn included, is a man; 'with no limits' trims HERE to its middle, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager is the person who runs and coordinates a business or team.

clue.text: One takes stock as gentleman recalled bare bottom

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so it is read in the opposite direction
stripped bare means its covering at each end is removed

parts.note: sir is the title for a gentleman
taken as written, then stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: A gentleman is called back after mooning someone, and someone takes stock of the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes stock' sounds like reviewing the situation, but here it is a dish that absorbs stock as it cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked by gradually adding stock, which the rice absorbs.

clue.text: Everyone can see this cutting comedic drama, Loot

indicators.note: cutting into something places a piece inside it
something comedic is played for laughs, so the letters are messed about

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A comedy-drama titled Loot is suitable viewing for all.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification meaning suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: To maraud is to raid and plunder, which is what looting means.

clue.text: Pull up in behind soldier

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the rear is the behind

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: to lug is to pull or haul something heavy

explanation.surface: An order to pull a soldier up from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional soldier in a standing army rather than a reservist.

clue.text: Makes attractive new games set in …

indicators.note: making something new means remaking these letters in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A new set of games makes things appealing, the ellipsis carrying the sentence on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this clue's surface to 23 across; 'set in' is part of the fodder, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To magnetise is literally to give something magnetic pull, and figuratively to attract or charm people.

clue.text: Time team cycling, identifying main changes?

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: cycling moves the first letter round to the end, like a wheel turning

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A time-trial cycling team spots shifts in the main event.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the open sea, so its changes are the rise and fall of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides are the regular rising and falling of the sea, the changes in the main.

clue.text: … space, taking singular, short, sharp breath

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside

parts.note: a gap is a space
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, outer space leaves one with a single quick intake of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasp is a sudden quick intake of breath in shock or effort.

clue.text: Focus for one securing wings for Grease cast

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside

parts.note: the Focus is an example of a Ford car

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two outermost letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone focused on getting a part, from the wings, in the cast of the musical Grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the show's performers, but here it is a verb meaning shaped in a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that is forged or cast has been shaped, by hammering or by pouring into a mould.

clue.text: Sweetheart's flat has nothing

indicators.note: one thing having another means it is followed by it here

parts.note: a surface that is true is level or flat
love is the tennis score for nothing

explanation.surface: A lover's apartment is completely empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A true love is a person's beloved, their darling or partner.

clue.text: Son occasionally parked in petrol station to get coffee

indicators.note: in places those pieces inside another

parts.note: Esso is a brand of petrol stations
S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A son, now and then, parks at a petrol station to grab a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is a strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Vacuous actor plugging body spray, gets speaking part?

indicators.note: plugging a gap means filling it from inside

parts.note: Lynx is a men's deodorant body spray, sold as Axe outside the UK

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside is cleared and only the outer letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An empty-headed actor advertising deodorant lands a speaking role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaking part' looks like an acting role; it is the part of the body that produces the voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx is the voice box, the organ in the throat that produces speech.
